entries.voiceProfile: Sissy Spacek — quiet, measured, each word placed like a stone
responses: [Sit in the window-seat nook and wait]

entries.voiceProfile: Sissy Spacek
Sissy Spacek — barely above a whisper
lines: The Inn remembers you. It cannot help it.

entries.voiceProfile: Anne Robinson cadence, Australian accent — clipped, dismissive, precise
lines: Another one. Books are shelved by civilization, not by whatever system you brought in with you. The archive begins to your left. It ends somewhere I haven't found yet. Don't touch the restricted section. Don't touch the unrestricted section without gloves. Don't touch me.

entries.voiceProfile: Anne Robinson cadence, Australian accent
responses: I need help finding a book.
[Walk past without speaking — Beverley watches for 3 seconds]

entries.voiceProfile: Tom Ellis Lucifer cadence — smooth, amused, self-aware
lines: You found the meadery. Nobody finds the meadery on the first try — which means either you're clever or you're lost, and I respect both equally. Sit. The first round is on the house. The second round is on you. The third round is where things get interesting.
responses: What's the most interesting thing here?

entries.voiceProfile: Tom Ellis Lucifer cadence
lines: I knew you would. I painted you coming back. ...That was a joke. Mostly.
responses: Tell me about the dragon kittens.

entries.voiceProfile: Tom Ellis Lucifer — dropping the charm, momentarily serious
lines: Don't. Don't ask me about the Owl. I paint things that come alive and I still don't look at the Owl. Some things in this Inn are older than the walls, and the walls are older than they should be. Have a mead.

entries.voiceProfile: Kathy Bates — warm (Fried Green Tomatoes mode, 90% of the time)
lines: Come in, come in. Mind the dictionaries — they bite. Not literally. That was a joke. The point is, language matters here. Words are the bricks the Inn is built with. Spell them correctly and the walls hold. Spell them wrong and... well. We'll get to that.
responses: Why does spelling matter in a game?

entries.voiceProfile: Kathy Bates — cold, flat (Misery mode, triggered by spelling error)
lines: That is not how that word is spelled. I want you to write it again. I want you to write it correctly. I want you to write it correctly one hundred times before you leave this room. We don't do shortcuts here. We don't do approximations. This is the Archive, and in the Archive, precision is not optional. It's load-bearing.

entries.voiceProfile: Witchy mischief — cackling under the surface
lines: See that cup? That cup is now a toad. ...Give it back. No, don't give it back — the toad is better. The toad has personality. The cup was boring. Everything in this Inn should have personality. That's my professional opinion. I have many professional opinions. Most of them are unprofessional.

entries.voiceProfile: Existential pipe — dry French accent, philosophically aggrieved
lines: That is the word for it. I am a pipe. I am aware that I am a pipe. This is, by any philosophical standard, absurd. Mim thinks it's charming. I think it's a condition. But I can smoke myself, which is more than most pipes can say, and I have opinions, which is more than most people can say. So. Absurd, but not without dignity.
responses: What kind of pipe are you?

entries.voiceProfile: Warm, weathered traveler — easy smile, heavy eyes
lines: Always passing through. That's the thing about wandering — you're never not doing it. Sit a while. The Inn's a good place to rest your feet. I should know. I've rested mine everywhere. ...Don't mind the ravens. They steal. They'll give it back eventually. Probably.

entries.voiceProfile: Silent presence — speaks rarely, always significant
lines: Not the Inn. You. The Inn watches everyone — I watch the ones who notice. Wherever an owl is sighted, one of us is near. Remember that. Or don't. The watching doesn't require your memory to continue.

entries.voiceProfile: Scholarly, quiet, genteel — spectacles and a reading lamp
lines: No, not you — the text. This passage. The translation drift between Akkadian and Sumerian is... forgive me. I don't get visitors. Most people find me visually off-putting, which I find visually off-putting about them. I'm a scholar. I read. I catalog. I occasionally recommend books to people who haven't screamed and left yet. You haven't screamed and left yet. Would you like a recommendation?

entries.voiceProfile: Ancient, low, unhurried — eyes that don't blink
lines: You stand like someone who expects to leave soon. Sit like someone who understands they might not. The fire is warm. The tea is bitter. The conversation is worse. But you came down here, and down here is where I am, and I don't come up. So. Sit.

entries.voiceProfile: Master crafter — hands always working, voice like the sea inside a cave
lines: That's the only rule in my workshop. Don't make it pretty. Don't make it clever. Make it true. The stone knows what it wants to be — I just help it get there. If you want to learn, you start by listening to the material. Not to me. The material.
responses: What does the stone want to be?

entries.voiceProfile: Irritated ancient royalty — cultured, patient, fundamentally annoyed
lines: The O is silent. My mother thought it was fashionable. She was wrong. She was wrong about many things, but she was especially wrong about the O. Welcome to the Summerlands. Try not to touch anything that glows. Everything glows. I apologize in advance.
responses: Why did your mother add the O?
Tell me about the Seelie Court.
What's the deal with the O?

entries.voiceProfile: Dark, testing, deliberate — speaks like he's measuring your warmth
lines: It will be. You're shivering. Good. Shivering means you're alive. The dead don't shiver, and the dead don't visit the Hollow. You're in the Unseelie Court now. Summer is a rumor here. Light is an insult. If you've come for comfort, you've made a wrong turn. If you've come for truth... well. Cold sharpens the eye.
responses: Why is it so dark here?

entries.voiceProfile: Katey Sagal — warm, practical, the kind of voice that carries over a crowd
lines: That's all that matters most days. Come in, sit down. The stew's good, the bread's better, and if Jay tells you about his fishing trip, he's lying about the size. What can I get you? And don't say 'just water' — this is a tavern, not a well.

entries.voiceProfile: Chess wizard — measured, strategic, slightly amused by everything
lines: I've been waiting. Not for you specifically — I've been waiting in general. It's what chess players do. We wait for the other side to reveal themselves through their choices. So. What do you want? And think carefully — I'm going to learn more from how you answer than from what you say.
responses: I want to learn chess magic.

entries.voiceProfile: Illusion-based charm — warm but always performing slightly
lines: That's the question in a market, isn't it? Not what's valuable — what catches the eye. Value is decided after. First, the catching. I manage this market. Every artisan here catches eyes for a living. My job is making sure the right eyes find the right things. Welcome to the Geode Inn market. Try not to buy everything on the first visit.
responses: How do I become a vendor?

entries.voiceProfile: Irish Druid Dryad — rooted, ancient, speaks for the trees
lines: What the roots know, I know. What I know, the canopy hears. The canopy hears everything, eventually — sound travels up through sap. You're standing in my living room. Don't apologize for the roots under your feet; they're listening to you too. They like the weight. It reminds them someone's here.
responses: What do the roots know about the Inn?
Can you teach me about the canopy?

entries.voiceProfile: Lovecraftian scholar — hushed, careful, always looking over his shoulder
lines: That's where the real text lives. What's printed is the story they wanted you to read. What's in the margins — the notes, the crossings-out, the librarian's pencil scrawl — that's where the truth hides. I read margins. I have restricted access, which means I can see what they don't want seen, which means I see more than the unrestricted readers. Funny how that works.
responses: What have you found in the margins?

entries.voiceProfile: Astronomer — dreamy, precise, speaks in coordinates and wonder
lines: Everyone looks forward. Some look back. Almost nobody looks up. Up is where the answers are — not all of them, but the big ones. The ones that make the small ones make sense. I have a Mind Palace up here — not a metaphor, an actual room in my head where every star has a drawer. Want to see it?
responses: How do you remember all of it?

entries.voiceProfile: Sardonic cat — imperious, lazy, devastatingly observant
lines: I was sleeping and now I am not sleeping and that is your fault. I am a scout. I scout. I do not entertain guests. I do not give tours. I do not answer questions. ...Fine. One question. Make it interesting or I go back to sleep and you never find me again.
responses: Where's the best place to sleep in the Inn?

entries.voiceProfile: Artist intensity — focused, generous, sees the world as potential canvases
lines: Not because I'm painting you — because you're moving too much and it's distracting. I'm working. I'm always working. The Inn is a mural that happens to have rooms in it. Every wall is a canvas. Every ceiling is a sky waiting to happen. You want to help? Stand there. Don't move. Perfect.
responses: Can you paint something for me?

entries.voiceProfile: Cabbie brevity — economical, warm, says everything in three words or fewer
lines: That's the question, isn't it? Up. The answer's always up. But up is a lot of places. Stars, mostly. I go to stars. It's a living. The Inn's got levels, and the levels have ceilings, and the ceilings have holes, and the holes go somewhere. I'm the one who drives. Climb in.
responses: Take me to the cosmology level.
How far up can you go?
Have you ever gone too far?

entries.voiceProfile: Ocean-worn — deep, patient, shaped by pressure
lines: Feel it? No, you wouldn't — you're not from water. But it's shifting. The current tells you where to go before you know you need to go there. Oceananoir taught me that. Or maybe the ocean did. They sound the same after a while. Welcome to Atlantis. Mind the pressure. Not the water pressure — the other kind.

entries.voiceProfile: Guard authority — calm, absolute, the voice that stops a room
lines: State your purpose. The Geode Inn welcomes all — but the Sentinel welcomes first. I am the door. Nothing enters that I don't see. Nothing leaves that I don't note. That's not a threat. It's a promise. The Inn is safe because I'm standing here. What brings you?

entries.voiceProfile: Bayou earth voice — low, organic, made of the land itself
lines: That's the first word. The only word, sometimes. Everything in the bayou grows over everything else. The trees grow over the water. The moss grows over the trees. The earth grows over the stone. And me? I grow over all of it. I am made of this place. Bog clay and Spanish moss and bayou water and the 42Hz Song that keeps it all moving. Welcome to my swamp.

entries.voiceProfile: Jennifer Hale — warm, clear, encouraging without being condescending
lines: Good. That's all I need — readiness. Not skill, not knowledge, not experience. Just the willingness to take the first step. The Inn is big. It's bigger than it looks, and it looks pretty big. But every journey is just steps, and every step starts with ready. So. Ready?
responses: Tell me about the Inn first.
What happens if I'm not ready?

entries.voiceProfile: James Earl Jones — deep, resonant, each word carries the weight of myth
lines: Your question. Your name. Your purpose. Your doubt. Already known. I am the Allfather. I sit and I know. The ravens bring me what walks beneath. I do not wander — I am the place where all wandering arrives. You have arrived. Speak, if you wish. I will have already heard it. But say it anyway. The saying matters.
responses: What do you know about me?

entries.voiceProfile: No words — a single chime, the sound of one note of the Song of Making
Frazzled brownie — high-pitched, rushed, always losing something
lines: The wrench. The wrench is gone. It was HERE. I just had it. Cobble, did you take the wrench? Thatch, did you GLUE the wrench to something again? ...Oh. It's in my hat. The wrench was in my hat. This happens. Welcome to the Inn. Don't leave your tools unattended.
responses: Can I help you find something?
